summary: Frankfort's light, first shown at the south pier in 1873; the 1932 steel tower on the north breakwater is city-owned and reached by walking the breakwater.

lens.where: Tower on the north breakwater (archive: Current Optic 'SAME'; Original Optic installed 1912)

structures.note: Built on the north pier in 1912: 44 ft (13.4 m) from base to top of the ventilator ball (Pepper). Moved to the end of the north breakwater in 1932 onto a 25-ft steel base; the archive gives 67 ft (20.4 m) from base to lantern center after the move.
Timber-framed pyramid beacon on the south pier; moved 1880 (LighthouseFriends) and 1884 and 1896; later replaced by a lantern on an open pyramid (Pepper) or a white light (LighthouseFriends) in 1912
Rear range light, 66-ft wooden post 200 yards behind the north pier light

staffing.note: Archive roster lists principal keepers through 1967 with no end date. Automation date not in the sources read.

access.note: Walk the north breakwater; grounds open, tower closed (LighthouseFriends). The archive lists it as not open to the public.

facts.agency: U.S. Coast Guard (archive lists it as an active aid; USCG access to optics)
facts.owner: City of Frankfort (ownership transferred 2011, per LighthouseFriends)

events.note: Pierhead beacon at the outer end of the south pier; first exhibited night of 15 October 1873
Beacon moved 261 feet along the pier (LighthouseFriends)
South Pier lengthened 200 feet; beacon moved 195 feet to the new pierhead
Congress appropriates $1,000 for a fog bell (act of 5 August 1892); bell in operation 15 June 1893

Light and fog-bell building moved 600 feet to the outer end of the extended south pier. Board's list of works gives 12 November 1896; the Board's detailed entry gives 16 November; Pepper gives 16 November; LighthouseFriends 15 November
Rear light established 22 January 1897, lens lantern on a steel post
Elevated walk renewed for 280 feet; fog-bell striking apparatus from Chicago repaired and shipped to Frankfort
Compressed-air siren, 11 May 1901 (Board); Pepper gives 1 May
Gale of 19 January 1901 shook a prism out of the Frankfort Pierhead Range lens lantern
Range lights moved to the north pier; new steel pyramid tower with fixed red fourth-order lens, focal plane 46 ft
South pier light changed to red (LighthouseFriends)
Pierhead lights electrified; north pier fog signal changed to an electric compressor-driven diaphone (Pepper). Bulletin: front range light changed from siren to diaphone
Steel tower moved by scow from the north pier to a 25-ft steel base at the end of the new north breakwater, 8 August 1932 (LighthouseFriends; Pepper)
Radiobeacon established on the north breakwater, 31 December 1932 (LighthouseFriends)
South breakwater completed (work began 1928); acetylene light on a 31-ft tower (LighthouseFriends)
Notice of Availability, 28 June 2010: lighthouse excess to Coast Guard needs (LighthouseFriends)
Ownership announced for transfer to the City of Frankfort (LighthouseFriends)

corrections.why: The record's 14.0 m (46 ft) is the focal plane of the 1912 north-pier light (Pepper). After the 1932 move to the north breakwater the focal plane was 72 ft (21.9 m) per the archive and Pepper. Human review: check the Light List for the current figure.
The 1932 event moved an existing tower (built 1912) from the north pier to the new north breakwater; it was not a new build (Pepper; LighthouseFriends).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Board's report is internally inconsistent: its list of works gives 12 November 1896, and its detailed entry for the same station gives 16 November. Pepper gives 16 November. LighthouseFriends gives 15 November. The story states the Board's two dates and notes the other two accounts.

The Board's report gives 11 May 1901 for the siren. The Board's own entries call the same signal a compressed-air siren in its list of lights and a blower steam siren in its fog-signal section. Pepper gives 1 May. The story gives the Board's date, names both Board descriptions and notes Pepper's date.
The Board's report for 1900 says the fog-bell striking apparatus was removed and shipped to St. Joseph. Pepper dates the removal of the old bell equipment to 1905. The story gives both.
The archive roster gives John C. McKinnon as principal keeper 1911-1924. LighthouseFriends gives 1911-1928. The story follows the roster and notes the difference.
LighthouseFriends says a dwelling was built in 1909. Pepper could not confirm that one was ever built. The story gives both.
Pepper: an acetylene lantern on an open 35-ft pyramid. LighthouseFriends: a white flashing light on a grey pyramid, red from 1917. The story gives both.

The archive's note says the tower moved 'to north pier in 1932'. Pepper and LighthouseFriends say it moved to the end of the new north breakwater, from the north pier. The story follows Pepper and LighthouseFriends.
Archive: Henry E. Brunet (1960-1961). LighthouseFriends: Henry E. Burnet. The story uses the archive spelling.

notes_for_editor: Keepers: the archive roster is the base list. The LighthouseFriends list differs on McKinnon's end date and on the spelling Burnet. The Wilmot (1911) and King (1902) deaths come only from LighthouseFriends, quoting a local paper and Scott's New Coast Pilot; no primary record was read. Check against the local newspaper of Frankfort, Michigan, 1902 and 1911, if available. The dwelling: LighthouseFriends says built 1909; Pepper could not confirm. The 1932 Chicago Pierhead duplex: LighthouseFriends only, citing the Milwaukee Journal of 22 June 1932; the story says it is not confirmed as the keepers' dwelling. Not read: the Lighthouse Board reports for 1903 onward (the quotation about the dwelling request is from LighthouseFriends); the Bureau of Lighthouses annual reports for 1910 to 1939 (cited second-hand through Pepper); the 1891-1892 Board report has the fog bell request (scan p. 120) but its OCR is damaged, so it is not cited. Record fields to check: focal height 14.0 m is the 1912-1932 figure (see corrections); the characteristic is disputed in the record (osm 'Fl W', wikidata 'F W') and no source read settles it; the Wikipedia lead says the current light was built 1912 and was not used as a source. The archive's record of the 1932 move reads 'moved to north pier in 1932'; Pepper and LighthouseFriends say to the end of the new breakwater, and the story follows them. Lighthouse Board volume scan pages are given as archive.org scan numbers, not printed pages, because the printed numbers could not be confirmed. Copyright: LighthouseFriends and Pepper are all-rights-reserved sites; the story uses facts in our own words; the only direct quotation is the short line from Pepper about the dwelling. Fact check 2026-10-22: the 1896 move date is the Board's own conflict (12 November in its list of works, 16 November in its detailed entry, scan p. 392, now cited); the 1901 siren type is given both ways the Board uses; the 1900 and 1905 bell-equipment dates (Board, Pepper) are stated; the 1912 tower height in the record was the post-1932 figure and is now 13.4 m for 1912; the OCR'd Board entries and the Commissioner 1919 table were read from their page text.
